title: lmvideo books
description: Learn to draw images, build scenes and render video with authored examples and locally verified showcases.

blocks.text: Install the lmctl command runner with npm install -g @lmctl-ai/lmctl. Read the source before running downloaded programs, then use a fresh directory for outputs. This first example uses a released lmvideo host declared by its source.

groups.title: CPU Cycles
groups.summary: Render the same authored scene with a CPU path tracer, as a still and a video.

blocks.text: Raster is the fast preview path. The same scene can use CPU Cycles for final lighting, reflections and roughness. Use the lmvideo 0.1.38 prerelease runtime.

Save each displayed source at its named examples/book/ path before running its compile/render commands. The output below is the structured result from the locked chapter capture; timing fields describe that historical run and vary on another machine.

blocks.alt: A gold sphere lit against a dark background.
blocks.caption: A CPU Cycles still shows lighting and reflections on a curved surface.
Forty-eight frames rendered by CPU Cycles at 24 frames per second. The still above is the chapter poster, not a frame from the clip.

blocks.text: The seven render_image arguments are width, height, renderer name, samples, maximum bounces, repeatable seed and denoise. A build without Cycles must report an error rather than silently render with raster. Video generation compiles once and renders each frame; these captures are local verification evidence, not a new website benchmark run.

groups.title: Migrating from the legacy hosts
groups.summary: Move lmdraw, lmmagnum, lmfilament and lmimg scripts to the canonical lmvideo schema with the structured migration tool: mechanical rewrites where the mapping is exact, located diagnostics where it is not.

chapters.title: Migrating from lmdraw, lmmagnum, lmfilament and lmimg

blocks.text: The legacy hosts are maintenance-only. The migration tool rewrites their _lmcode_ blocks to canonical lmvideo, or prints path:line:col diagnostics with stable LMV7xxx codes for what cannot migrate. Nothing is rewritten silently: every transformation is recorded in the JSON report, and approximate mappings are warnings, not surprises.

Run: python3 scripts/migrate-legacy.py old-script.lms -o migrated.lms --report report.json. Blocks with errors stay byte-identical and keep running on their pinned legacy host; --keep-going writes the partially migrated file. The full per-method rule table is --list-rules.

Highlights: lmdraw diagrams map one-to-one (scene.X -> canvas.X); lmimg image operations keep names, units and centisecond GIF delays; lmmagnum keeps vertical-FOV cameras, negates light directions into lmvideo's toward-the-source convention and converts float colors to sRGB hex; lmfilament's .filamat material compilation is a deliberate diagnostic, not a fake. See the docs/book/migrating-from-legacy-hosts.md chapter for the complete tables.

Worked example, lmmagnum to lmvideo: the first script runs on the pinned legacy host; the second is the migration tool's reviewed output running on lmvideo (declared-equivalent geometry, camera and colors; the GGX PBR lighting differs from the Blinn-Phong preview by design).
